name: Colorado

context: CO 340 and 603: wind erosion is a stated purpose of cover crops and herbaceous wind barriers on Colorado cropland.
cover_rules: CO 340: the minimum number of days a cover crop must grow after emergence and prior to termination is 30 days.
CO 340: do not harvest cover crops for seed.
CO 340: for late spring to fall seeded crops, terminate cover crops 35 days or earlier or 15 days or earlier, depending on the zone in the termination guidelines.
residue: CO 329: the crop interval STIR value shall be no greater than 20.
CO 329: keep stubble at least 10 inches for row spacing of less than 15 inches, or at least 15 inches for 15 inches or greater, while significant snowfall is expected.
CO 345: the crop interval STIR value shall be no greater than 80, and no moldboard plow-type primary inversion tillage.
barriers: CO 589: trap strips at least 15 feet wide if vegetation is one foot or more in height, at least 25 feet wide if less than one foot.
CO 585: include a minimum of two strips within the area prone to wind erosion.
CO 588: space cross wind ridges no more than four times the designed height of the ridges.
roughening: CO 609: emergency tillage should produce random roughness large enough for a 25% reduction in potential erosion rate.
grazing: CO 528: plan grazing to provide adequate ground cover from plant canopy, litter and trampled residue to reduce wind and water detachment.
CO 528: minimize grazing animal impact on areas that have high soil erosion potential.
drought: CO 528: develop and document contingencies for episodic disturbances such as drought.
seeding: CO 550: calculate seeding rates on a pure live seed (PLS) basis.
CO 550: rest range plantings from grazing from the date of seeding for at least two successive growing seasons.
dunes: CO 342: plants for sand dunes must survive burial by blowing sand; include sand trapping devices such as sand fences or brush matting.
